objects.description: Opaque handle type for a TEN VAD (voice activity detection) instance. It represents an implementation-defined object managed via the provided create/process/destroy API. Treat it as an opaque pointer; do not dereference or assume layout.

functions.name: ten_vad_create
functions.signature: TENVAD_API int ten_vad_create(ten_vad_handle_t *handle, size_t hop_size, float threshold);
functions.description: Create and initialize a TEN VAD instance. On success, writes an opaque handle to *handle. The hop_size defines the frame step (in samples) expected by subsequent processing calls. The threshold sets the decision boundary for classifying voice activity based on the computed probability (>= threshold => voice). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: handle must be a non-null pointer to storage for a ten_vad_handle_t; on success it will be assigned a valid handle.
hop_size is the number of samples between frame starts; it must be a positive value and must match the audio_data_length used in ten_vad_process.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates error and no usable handle.
A successfully created handle must be released with ten_vad_destroy to avoid resource leaks.

functions.name: ten_vad_process
functions.signature: TENVAD_API int ten_vad_process(ten_vad_handle_t handle, const int16_t *audio_data, size_t audio_data_length, float *out_probability, int *out_flag);
functions.description: Process one audio frame for voice activity detection using a previously created VAD handle. Writes the probability of voice activity to out_probability in [0.0, 1.0] and a binary decision to out_flag (0: no voice, 1: voice), where the decision uses the threshold configured at creation. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Note: The comment mentions ten_vad_init(), but no such function exists in this header; it likely refers to ten_vad_create().
requirements: handle must be a valid ten_vad_handle_t previously returned by ten_vad_create and not yet destroyed.
audio_data must be a non-null pointer to int16_t samples.
audio_data_length must equal the hop_size provided to ten_vad_create.
out_probability must be a non-null pointer to writable float storage (at least 1 element). On success, value will be in [0.0, 1.0].
out_flag must be a non-null pointer to writable int storage (at least 1 element). On success, value will be 0 or 1 (1 iff out_probability >= threshold).
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates error.
The input buffer must contain exactly one analysis frame corresponding to the configured hop size; sample format is 16-bit signed PCM.

functions.name: ten_vad_destroy
functions.description: Destroy a TEN VAD instance and release its resources. On return, sets *handle to NULL. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: handle must be a non-null pointer to a ten_vad_handle_t obtained from ten_vad_create.
*handle must be a valid, currently active handle that has not already been destroyed.
After successful return, *handle is set to NULL and must not be used in further calls.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates error.

functions.name: ten_vad_get_version
functions.description: Retrieve the TEN VAD library version string (e.g., "1.0.0"). Intended for diagnostics, logging, or feature gating. The returned string should be treated as read-only.
requirements: The returned const char* points to a read-only, null-terminated string; do not modify or free it.
Pointer validity/lifetime is not explicitly documented; assume it remains valid for typical library lifetime.

data_types.description: A buffer representing a single frame of signed 16-bit little-endian PCM audio samples. The buffer length is exactly hop_size samples (hop_size provided during VAD creation). Each sample is an int16 value; no header or container format, just raw PCM data.
